steps.name: Leone
steps.text: ♪She spread her arms, spread her heart, showed me that pretty face♪

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: ♪And from that moment on, I found my dreams in her embrace♪

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I still remember when you fellas got together to sing that, back in the day. Your voices lit up the entire room... Felt like your singing cleared up the winter fog that year.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Always the same song as just now, ma'am?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Haha, hardly. They knew all sorts of songs. The miners came from all over, bringing so many songs in so many languages.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Umm... Does Woodrow also know how to sing?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: He ain't much of a talker. Whenever we all get together, he just stuffs his face. Like now.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... Helena, when are you gonna crack open the bottle of champagne I brought back?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Shoot, I really am getting old, huh? Nearly forgot.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Umm, about Miles... He...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Don't worry about him. Said he wanted to take a stroll, so he did.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Just pop the cork and pour him a glass. We can toast when he comes back!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Alright, without further ado—

The cork shoots out with a pop, golden wine and silver foam splashing out at the same time. The sweet aroma spreads across the room, and wondrous befuddlement sparkles in the eyes of everyone at the table.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Here, Jessica, you're the star tonight, so the first glass is for you.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Thank you...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Next up is you, Woody. Thanks for helping her talk some sense into that stubborn old burdenbeast.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Don't mention it.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: This one's for Miles... This one's for me... And last and definitely least is you, Leone. For killing us with worry all this time.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Okay, I deserved that.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: To be perfectly honest, I actually—

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: If you got something to say, better wait for Miles. You ain't gonna leave him out like that, are you?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Ah, yeah, makes sense.
The table that had been lively all evening falls quiet, and the spilled champagne seeps silently into dark, unseen places.
Past bowls and plates.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Excuse me...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: What is it, Benny?
Past cups and saucers.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Actually... there's something I wanted to announce to everyone...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Was wondering why you were so quiet today, but I guess you had something brewing. Waiting to snatch the spotlight from your dad at the dinner table?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Benny, why don't you wait for Miles too?
Past empty wine bottles.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: No... I think now's the best time.
Until it flows over the table's edge, and seeps into the floor.
Snap.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: I'm leaving.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Hah, guess you finally got sick of us noisy old farts. Can't you wait for Miles to get back, so we can share one last drink before we say goodbye?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: No... I meant I'm leaving Davistown.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Look at this kid, getting drunk without touching a drop of champagne.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: No, I'm perfectly sober.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: It's something I've been meaning to get off my chest... But I never got the chance, so I'm saying it now.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: What's wrong? Why's everyone look like it just started raining?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Miles, I...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Benny just said... that he wants to leave Davistown.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Wh-What?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: How long you been thinking about this, boy?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: About a year or so...

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Last month, Ms. Selena from next door came over and said that her daughter in Ironforge City managed to find a caravan willing to come through here. She said she was planning to go with it to follow her daughter.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: She asked if I wanted to come. She thought it'd be a waste of my talents to stay. No matter how much I learn here, I wouldn't have a place to use any of it.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: She told me... she didn't want me to become the next Sylvia.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: What about your living expenses? Tuition? Where are you gonna live?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Don't worry, there are plenty of boarding schools in Ironforge City willing to provide scholarships so I can study there.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Benny... why wait so long to discuss this with us? It's a big decision... You know better than that.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, Miles.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: He ain't asking for our input.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Just letting us know the decision he's made.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...Have you thought this through? Weighed the pros and cons? Who knows, this place might perk up once it gets moving again. You can always decide then.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: I don't want to wait that long.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: The only reason you're all willing to stay put and pray things get better is because you remember the good old days.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: But I don't. This place has been a dump for as long as I can remember.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: ...My adoptive father worked so hard for this place, throwing away everything else without hesitation. My brother took his place as a pillar of the family, and wanted to join a mercenary group when he came of age. To earn money to send back home.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: But a few years later... Those people sent his belongings back, with no explanation in the attached letter except a few lines saying they're sorry.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: There should've been another path for him back then. Just like... there should be one for me now.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: ....Am I wrong?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: So when are you leaving?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: ...Tomorrow. I know I shouldn't have waited this long to tell you, but if I don't say it now... I'll never get another chance.
The boy glances across the table at his father, mustering the courage to look him in the eyes. He desperately hopes to see anger and resentment.
That would make him feel a little less guilty, a little less conflicted.
But his father simply hangs his head and remains silent, completely at a loss for words.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Leone...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: It's fine... It'll be alright...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: It's not a bad idea...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: You should leave... You deserve it...
Helena gives Leone a few pats on the shoulder, but he simply continues to mechanically repeat a few words of approval, prompting her to shake him a bit harder.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: It's fine, Helena. I'll be alright... This is how it should be...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Then, I wish you a safe journey. Take care of yourself, kid.
Why's it so damn cold here?
I picked up some wood we can burn. Feel any better yet?
Judging from how you curled up into a ball, I'm guessing you've never been through anything like this? *sigh*... How could your folks think you'd make it as a mercenary?
Huh? You decided on it yourself? But why? Did you get in a fight with your family?
Oh... There are people you want to protect, and problems you want to solve, huh? Mm, sounds pretty ambitious, if you ask me. I'm a bit jealous, to be honest.
Most people you see out here in these ruins, on the battlefield, were pushed here by circumstance. Myself included.
Driven by poverty. By injustice. By darkness and violence. We often pick up our weapons and rashly open fire, without worrying about what we're aiming at.
Right up until we finally step in a puddle of mud and look down at our footprints, only to realize that what we just stepped in... was a river of blood.
When that happens, I'm sure there's some noble ideal that can keep you from collapsing in defeat. Too bad I never found out what it was... I was only in it for the money.
My family owes a lot of money. And my little brother, well, he's damn smart. If he'd been born rich, he'd be at the top of his class.

spans.text: of money. And my little brother, well, he's damn smart. If he'd been born rich, he'd be at the top of his class.

steps.text: But if he stays back home... the only future he's got is as a debt collector.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... I don't think that counts as being in it only for the money. You're doing it for your family... That's noble too.
Eh, who can say? But for now at least...
We're doing it just to survive.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: The attack's about to begin...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Stop drinking already, Leone.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: ...Can I sleep at the diner tonight?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: If you want.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: (*whispers*) Poor fella... Just look at him... *sigh*...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: (*whispers*) It's just like seven years ago...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: What, you guys gonna talk about Carl now? Don't mind me. No need to tiptoe around it.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: This is already the second time... The second time...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Twice now... So why're you avoiding me? You think... you think I can't handle it?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Thank you for bringing me here, Jessica. You can head back now.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... still don't feel very good about this.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: I don't think your boss would be happy with how you're always fretting over us.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I just... can't bear to stand on the sidelines when there's something I can do.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Still, you helped Dad keep the house, so thanks again.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But the reason he finally sold his shares... was because of you.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: I know. He had to give up what was most precious to him just to keep a roof over my head. But with me gone, he'll finally be free to do what he really wants.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: In that sense, the house was never the obstacle. It was me and my brother.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: ...Do you remember my brother?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: You're talking about Carl? I've heard you and Helena mention him before.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Yeah, we know him as Carl... But over at Blacksteel, he went by a codename—Blackplate.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Blackplate?

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: It's water under the bridge, Leone. Why dredge it up now...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: No point trying to stop him, Miles. Just let him talk. He never brought it up, so we didn't say nothing. But now that he wants to look back, it's our job to let him.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: ...I suppose.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: I didn't ask for these thoughts... But in the dead of night, do I really have any control over what pops into my head?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: The more I dwelled on it, the more painful it was. The more painful it was, the less it made sense... But, Benny figured that all out a long time ago.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: He was right. Every step Carl took was never really his own choice. Because I was too stubborn, too arrogant. I ended up running everything dry... our money, our lives, and our choices.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: When I was little, there was a miner who'd always complain how nothing was easy anymore when you're middle-aged. You run outta energy and can only focus on a few things at a time.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: So you gotta be smart, gotta keep your eyes on what really matters. Stop being greedy.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: But when it was my turn to grow old, I just refused to accept it. I grabbed the wrong end of the rope, and held on for dear life. Told myself I was a brave warrior, fighting the good fight against fate itself...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: And what do I have to show for it?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Fought my way into a mountain of debt. Fought for a Davistown on its last legs. Fought for my eldest to die on the battlefield. My second son saw right through me, so why wouldn't he run the hell away?!

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Leone, we all know how much the mine means to you...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Then tell me, how much?! Because I haven't a damn clue at this point!

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: All I know is that I should've held onto those little hands back then. The hands of my children...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: I was a damn fool. How could I not see the writing on the walls when I heard that complaint?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: I should've etched those words into my mind...

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: My dad might be an old fool with the memory of a sieve, but I'm not.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: I recognized you the moment I saw you. The emblem on your uniform and your gear. It's the exact same one I saw on the bag with Carl's personal affects.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: He... He was your brother... I never realized...

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Did he never tell you his real name? Or did you simply forget all about him?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I remember him... I didn't work with him for very long, but how could I forget?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: You actually worked with Carl?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: In Chernobog. We were left together to scout out the strength of the enemies hidden in the ruins... I was there when he was injured. I-I was so flustered at the time, my mind went completely blank. I-I...

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: You were there when he died.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Y-Yes... I was.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: But you still didn't know his real name.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Actually...

a.text: Actually, the time I spent with him was very short.
Actually, I was so scared back then that I barely remember a thing.
Actually, mercenaries always keep a few secrets close to their hearts, that they don't readily disclose to others.
Actually... there is no 'actually' at all. Jessica knows this very well.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: It's alright. That wasn't the point I was trying to make.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: What I wanted to know is, have you ever seen a silver ring inlaid with diamonds?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: It belonged to his biological mother, and he always carried it with him. But it wasn't in the bag sent back by your company.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: If you watched him die... then surely you know what happened to it. Were you the one who took it? If so, give me back my brother's things.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No... I-I have no idea. I've never seen him with a ring like that... Maybe it got lost.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: ...How could Carl possibly lose that ring?

steps.name: Bored Bank Employee
steps.text: Finally done with the last one... Let's take a look. Oho, number 120.

steps.name: Indifferent Bank Employee
steps.text: With just a few strokes of the pen, a hundred and twenty people have been sent to the frontier.

steps.name: Bored Bank Employee
steps.text: Well, you better keep that pen moving or you'll be next.

steps.name: Indifferent Bank Employee
steps.text: Sylvia, mind getting the lights? I'm going to go lie down for a sec.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: A hundred and twenty people...
Sylvia's stress and anxiety make her habitually reach up to fumble around her collar. As soon as she feels the familiar ring resting atop her chest, she hastily gives it a squeeze.
The ring's unyielding texture digs into her palm, yet gradually calms her down as well.
Just like that embrace seven years ago. It was so tight she couldn't breathe, yet it eventually placated her surging tears.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Carl... What should I do?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: What else... is there for me to do...?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Since you don't know where it is... Head back, Jessica. Thanks for sending me off.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Honestly, I'm grateful that you convinced Dad to choose the house. Now, even if I decide to leave... he won't be left with nothing.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: At the end of the day, those shares did nothing but make him feel a bit better. Not a damn thing.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: If... If he ultimately wasn't able to keep the house, w-would you still have chosen to leave?

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: ...I don't know. I don't want to be an obstinate fool, but... I don't want to be an ingrate either.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Alright, this is goodbye for real, Jessica.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Why are you still following me? What do you hope to accomplish? What can you even do at this point?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I-I'm not sure myself... All I know is... I don't think you should leave like this.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Please, go back already. I'm begging you.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: You're holding a golden nail in your hand. It's extremely valuable, but... please don't use it to repair paper houses.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: In the end, no matter how hard you work at it, all you'll be left with are a few extra holes.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Paper that thin will crumble under its weight anyway.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Go back to where you belong, the house swathed in silver and gold. Find a place where you can drive that nail in. That's where it truly belongs.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: So please, just stop following me. Alright?
Has Benny gone back yet?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Yes, Woodrow. I saw him home.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Then why ain't you heading back, too?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I won't be able to fall asleep even if I do. I wanted a little bit of time to myself.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: What the hell did that brat say to you?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Just something... very reasonable. It reminded me of...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It reminded me of a few things. A few things I should've already known.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Ever since I was little, helping others was like grabbing a little yellow toy fowlbeast in a crystal-clear bathtub. All I had to do was extend my hand, and I'd be able to prevent the tub from spilling over.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But that's because the faucet built with the wealth and authority bestowed to me only dispensed the warmest, clearest water. That's why everything around me always looked so pristine.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But as soon as I stepped out from that bathtub, from my family circle, I came face-to-face with... reality.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Reality is a murky quagmire. When you reach in, you have no idea what you'll pull out. Or what you'll touch.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: There's no reason for you to agonize over this.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: To be blunt, nothing you did meant a damn thing to Benny's final decision.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I watched that kid grow up. He's been full of good ideas since he was little. Great ideas. He...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: He really takes after someone I once knew. When he sorts things out in his head and makes up his mind, he'll set off in a straight line and never look back. He'll clear a path forward, but no way back.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sounds like... an extremely determined person. Almost irrationally so.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Hardly. He was the most rational person I know: the source of all our problems, as well as the solutions, can only be found on the road ahead of us.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... I'm a bit jealous of people like that. Being that perceptive at a young age must save you a lot of unnecessary detours.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Don't ever envy people for that, Jessica.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Why do you say that?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Because they'll end up bald. Not a single strand of hair.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Thanks for the reassurance.
